Hi Maya (and team),

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier — Aurora’s infra and data governance teams are aligned to proceed with a 4-week evaluation. Procurement asked us to capture a short mutual action plan (MAP) that lists the technical handoffs so they can attach an internal PO milestone schedule.

High level asks from our side to include in the MAP:
- A test tenant / org seeded with a read-only service account for our engineers (name: aurora-test-redwood)
- Short-lived API keys for developers (ephemeral TTL preference: 8 hrs) and guidance on rotation
- IP allowlist entry for our staging CIDR (10.45.128.0/20) and a proposed maintenance window for VPC peering (we prefer a weekend)
- A minimal network diagram showing ports/egress for inference calls and KV/caching (we typically allow 443 and some metadata 8443)

Can you add owners and due dates so procurement can align on the contract gating (PO + SOW)? I attached a one‑page template (Aurora-MAP_v0.3.xlsx) for your convenience.

If useful, procurement@aurorahealth.io will accept calendar invites for a short alignment call this week.

Best,
Samantha Lee
Director of Platform Integrations
Aurora Health

Samantha — thanks, this is great. We can definitely land the MAP and owners today. Below is a concise action list I propose; I’ve put tentative internal owners and target dates (all in PDT):

Immediate mutual-action items (POC / 4-week evaluation):
- Seed test org & create service account (aurora-test-redwood) — owner: maya_srinivasan — target: 2026-03-30 17:00
- Issue ephemeral developer API keys + rotation doc (TTL: 8h, default) — owner: priyom_das — target: 2026-03-31 12:00
- Coordinate IP allowlist + confirm staging CIDR (10.45.128.0/20) — owner: rishi_malhotra — target: 2026-04-02 10:00
- VPC peering window proposal + pre-checks (weekend of Apr 10-11) — owner: rishi_malhotra — target: 2026-04-03 09:00
- Provide minimal network diagram and firewall/egress requirements — owner: maya_srinivasan — target: 2026-03-30 12:00
- DocuSign MAP & SOW: we’ll upload signed copy once Aurora confirms PO date — owner: sales ops — target: 2026-04-05

Notes / technical clarifications:
- We can support either classic VPC peering or a PrivateLink-style connection. Peering gives lower latency but requires route adjustments; PrivateLink avoids routes but needs an ENI in your subnet. Rishi — I’ll defer to you for a recommendation given Aurora’s security posture.
- API keys: we’ll issue short-lived keys scoped to inference + embeddings; longer lived service keys (rotation policy) are available if you require non-ephemeral automation.
- For the test org we’ll enable request-level audit logs and provide a simplified role (read/generate) for the test account.

I attached our network diagram for your team’s network folks to review (redwood-network-diagram.png). I also filled a draft of the MAP in your spreadsheet and will upload the signed MAP to DocuSign once procurement confirms PO timing.

Next step: small alignment call tomorrow 10:00 PDT to confirm peering window and API key approach? If that works I’ll send invite to procurement@aurorahealth.io.

Thanks — Maya
Maya Srinivasan

Redwood Inference

On Sun, Mar 29, 2026 at 11:03, maya_srinivasan <maya@redwood.inference> wrote:
> - VPC peering window proposal + pre-checks (weekend of Apr 10-11) — owner: rishi_malhotra — target: 2026-04-03 09:00

Quick technical notes from my side for Aurora engineers and your security team:
- Ports: outbound 443 to our inference endpoints is sufficient. If you plan to run KV caching over a separate endpoint we will call that over 8443 — allow these to our public service CIDRs.
- CIDR allowlist: confirm whether Aurora NAT egress uses the staging CIDR (10.45.128.0/20) for all envs; if ephemeral dev boxes exist please provide any additional ranges.
- Peering vs PrivateLink: given Aurora’s security constraints, PrivateLink is safer (no route table changes) but requires an ENI in your VPC and a small config change. If you want lower-latency token throughput for tight SLAs choose peering; for isolation/approved audit surface choose PrivateLink.
- Certificate pinning: we support standard TLS with rotation; if you require mTLS we can enable it but that adds ~2 days to the window for cert exchange and testing.

I recommend we block Apr 10 (Sat) 02:00–06:00 PDT for the peering maintenance window (low traffic). If Aurora prefers a different timezone, we can adapt.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

A couple of quick items from Aurora:
- We prefer PrivateLink because our network team wants minimal route changes. Please send the steps for ENI creation and required IAM role mapping.
- Ephemeral key TTL of 8 hours is fine; can you include a short snippet for automatic rotation (example: curl -> vault -> redwood ephemeral) in the rotation doc?
- Please confirm whether audit logs will be available in the Redwoods Console for the test org and how long logs are retained (default retention we saw in the docs was 30 days).

We’re happy to take the 10:00 PDT call tomorrow — procurement invited an SRE and a security reviewer.

Samantha Lee
